A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same RCCDA research work, with all 45 pages, Appendices A-G, and the checklist available. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that differences are confined to pages 1, 18, and 19.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification, update-rate, computational-overhead, robustness, and replay-buffer experiments in Section 6 and Appendices D and F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including evaluations on PACS, DigitsDG, OfficeHome, and MEMD-ABSA.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the gain estimator, virtual-queue update threshold, model updates, and Appendix F.6 replay-buffer extension are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four datasets and tasks, seven drift schedules, and supplementary noisy-loss and recurring-drift scenarios. No coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Uniform Random, Periodic, Budget-Increase, and Budget-Threshold remain the policy comparators. Appendix D.2 retains the same ADWIN and KS-Test timing comparisons.

E3.justification: The data splits, preprocessing, architectures, evaluation procedures, resource constraints, and hyperparameters in Section 6 and Appendix E are identical, as are the supplementary experimental settings.

E4.justification: The resource analyses, cross-domain evaluation, update-rate sensitivity, noisy-loss robustness, replay-buffer comparison, and per-domain result breakdown in Appendices D and F are retained without revision.

E5.justification: Seed counts, averaging procedures, standard-deviation reporting, and Appendix F.7's statistical-significance discussion are identical. Neither version adds runs or changes uncertainty reporting relative to the other.

E6.justification: All numerical results and reported findings are unchanged. For example, RCCDA remains at 72.8 ± 4.5% on PACS Burst in Table 1 and 81.4 ± 2.9% on MEMD-ABSA Burst in Table 11.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 removes the inference-batch-independence rationale supporting step (d). It retains the conditional-independence assertion and identical factorization, so this is a localized reduction in proof justification. All formal assumptions, equations, and theorem statements remain unchanged; the B.2 edit is grammatical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about convergence analysis, resource-constrained update policy design, and empirical effectiveness.

C2.justification: Interpretations of drift adaptation and resource utilization are unchanged, as are qualifications concerning estimator error, weaker benefits under modest drift, and the adaptation-versus-retention tradeoff with replay.

D1.justification: Appendices E and G retain identical architecture descriptions, hyperparameters, software versions, hardware, execution instructions, timing information, and code/data access disclosures.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are identical, including the distinctions from drift detection, domain generalization, and continual learning.

P1.justification: v3 shortens the explanation of proof step (d) in B.1, corrects 'The drift-induced loss term can related' to 'We can relate the drift-induced loss term' in B.2, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Document organization is unchanged.

P2.justification: The shortened proof passage causes small vertical-spacing and text-reflow changes on page 18. All figures, tables, captions, and their placement remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects one grammatical sentence and shortens a proof justification, providing slight editorial cleanup while making the independence rationale less explicit. The mathematical statements, empirical evidence, claims, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, yielding no meaningful net difference in overall quality.
